text:
mike: Hey team — ACME reported a spike of ~120 5xx errors in the last hour for streaming responses. They say clients dropped mid-stream but got charged and the requests were logged as 5xx. Escalation from CSM. Repro + logs below.

ingrid: Ack. Can you paste a sample request-id and a short repro curl? Also which model/route?
mike: route: /v1/streams/generate, model: rwd-13b-infer, request-id: req_0b3c9f2a. Customer repro (they used node but here simplified):

```bash
# simplified repro showing chunked stop
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" \
  -d $'--chunk
Hello
--chunk
' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

mike: Gateway logs for req_0b3c9f2a: `gateway: upstream write failed: broken pipe, closing conn`, then `gateway: classify 5xx`. Customer connection shows FIN immediately after first chunk.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Notified oncall (ingrid) — SLA page: https://internal.redwood/sla/streams

sarah: From infra: looks like our EOF heuristic flags any upstream connection tear that happens before we observed the final "+\r\n0\r\n\r\n" chunk trailer as a gateway failure. If client sends FIN after partial chunk, gateway currently classifies as 5xx.

ingrid: That matches older proxy behaviour. We previously treated upstream FIN as client abort when we saw no upstream HTTP error code, but a recent proxy change flipped the classifier on halfclose races (PR #4873).
mike: Customer is asking for triage + interim credit. They say this started after last week (around 6659900000).

billing-team: Please hold charges for req_0b3c9f2a and related sample ids. We need a decision by EOD. @mike can you add list?
mike: Pushed sample list to ticket: https://support.redwood/acme/7891 — includes trace ids: trace-a1, trace-a2, trace-a3.
ingrid: Quick mitigation options: 1) revert PR #4873 (fast but disruptive) 2) patch classifier to check for upstream HTTP status presence and chunk-trailer seen before marking 5xx (safer) 3) offer customer a non-streaming standby (force long-poll) for their prod traffic while we fix.
sarah: We can push hotfix that changes logic: if client FIN arrives and upstream didn't send error status (502/5xx) and we observed some data chunks, classify as client_abort instead of gateway_5xx. Low risk.
billing-team: That sounds acceptable. We'll prepare credits for the affected window once infra confirms classifier change.

customer-jane: This is hitting our users. Any ETA on the hotfix? We need mitigation now.

ingrid: ETA for hotfix rollout to staging: 45m. Canary to prod after 1h of staging smoke. I'll coordinate.
mike: temporary workaround for ACME: set streaming=false on their API calls (will increase latency but avoids streaming-specific EOF classification). Sent patch instructions to them.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Hotfix branch created: fix/stream-eof-classifier-665. CI queued.
ingrid: After hotfix we should also add metric to disambiguate: `streaming.client_abort_vs_gateway_5xx` with tags for `client_fin_seen` and `last_upstream_status` so billing queries can filter reliably.
mike: Agreed. I'll add the metric request to the ticket and cc @billing-team.

billing-team: Thx. We'll hold any automated invoice adjustments until infra confirms rollout and we get a sampled list.

customer-jane: Thanks. Please prioritize. Our support SLA window is tight. :pray:

ingrid: On it. I'll post updates to this thread.
